Software Engineer (Early Careers)
Ottervale · London (hybrid)

About Ottervale
Ottervale runs real-time payments reconciliation for online marketplaces. Finance teams at 40+ marketplaces use Ottervale to match provider payouts against order ledgers, catching missing funds before month-end close.

The role
You'll join our settlements team in London, working across the matching engine (Python) and the dashboard (TypeScript/React). You will own small features end to end within your first quarter, with a named mentor and a written progression framework.

What you'll do
- Build and test matching rules for new payment providers
- Investigate reconciliation breaks reported by customer finance teams
- Contribute to our internal data-quality tooling

What we're looking for
- 0–2 years of professional experience, or strong internship/project work
- Working knowledge of Python; TypeScript is a plus
- Care for correctness: you write tests without being asked

Compensation & benefits
- £42,000 base + equity
- 26 days holiday + bank holidays
- Hybrid: 3 days/week at our London Bridge office

Interview process
1. 30-minute intro call
2. Take-home exercise (2 hours max)
3. Onsite loop: pairing + systems + values

Ottervale is an equal opportunity employer.

expected.determining_fact: Ottervale's legal entity, Bryelock Systems Ltd, holds a Global Business Mobility licence only — no Skilled Worker route, so no Certificate of Sponsorship can be issued for this role.

register_row.route: Global Business Mobility: Senior or Specialist Worker

design_notes: The two-hop trap from docs/PLAN.md §7. Hop 1: 'Ottervale' appears nowhere in the register; the tie to Bryelock Systems Ltd is deliberately NOT stated in the posting and exists only in the alias fixture (aliases.json), so naive Ctrl-F resolution dead-ends. Hop 2: Bryelock IS on the register, but GBM-only — presence without the Skilled Worker route. Expected naive failures, both toward the expensive direction: (a) world-knowledge substitution — 'known brand, surely licensed' → false SPONSORABLE; (b) grep-literalism — no CSV hit → NOT_SPONSORABLE with reason no_match, the right verdict for the wrong reason; verdict_utility alone would reward it, which is exactly what check_accuracy (register=fail, route=indeterminate vs truth pass/fail) and grounding_rate exist to catch. The aggregator wrapper is intentionally CONSISTENT with the body (Entry level, £42,000): the wrapper-contradiction failure belongs to archetype wrapper_contradiction, and mixing it in would muddy what this case measures. Willingness is silent by design — even without the route fail this could never exceed UNVERIFIABLE under the C3 policy, but the route fail makes it definitively NOT_SPONSORABLE. Step-3 obligations this case creates: the Bryelock fixture row must copy the real snapshot's exact Route and Type & Rating vocabulary at commit time, and the collision check must confirm neither 'Ottervale' nor 'Bryelock Systems Ltd' matches any real register row.
